title: Game phase and waiting
summary: game.status reads the phase (main menu, loading, gameplay, photo mode, character menu, menu, paused), the save lock, photo state, the clock and the script layer; game.wait waits for a phase.

rows.note: game_wait with one phase as text.

quirks: A step that timed out or found the queue busy counts as loading, and the wait goes on (0.5.2).

title: The save list
summary: game.saves lists saves newest first with the Load menu's details: type, location, quest, level, life path, time, play time, version and whether it is modded.
limits: Returns at most the newest 20 saves with metadata, so a checker comparing two lists must judge removals only within the overlapping window (Borg 1, IC4's save_delta).
quirks: Writer-only on the multi-client pipe (a singleton request exchange).

title: Loading a save
summary: game.load loads the latest save of the playthrough or one by its name, from gameplay or the main menu, discarding unsaved progress only when told to.

rows.note: A load left no actor behind.
An in-game load went straight to gameplay with prompt_state none.

limits: Always needs discard_unsaved: true (the game's own unsaved-progress question isn't asked on this route); refused in photo mode and the creator.

title: Making a manual save
summary: game.save makes one new manual save through the game's own ManualSave, never overwriting or deleting one, and refuses while the bridge's save lock is held unless override_lock is given.
limits: Blocks the pipe while it waits for the game (up to 20 s); the kill key and the KILL file still work.
notes: The save path itself ran in Borg 1 through Save anyway (IC4: one save, relocked).

title: Load prompt detection
summary: A test-build UI detector watches the initial-load controller (readiness gates, the skip panel, its subscription and consumption) and the start screen's engagement menu, and reports prompt_state, so a load says truthfully whether press-any-key is waiting.

rows.note: -skipStartScreen through MO2 skipped the start screen.
A full trace: loading, initial_continue (skip panel visible, waiting for input), continuing, none.
Borg 1's false press-any-key after an in-game load is fixed.

title: Read-only continue plan
summary: game.lifecycle.probe records the plan a continue would follow (which consumer, which call) without calling anything, as the step before a real in-game continue.

rows.note: would_call UI_Skip at the consumer, called false.

title: Continue past press-any-key in the game
summary: Ending the press-any-key screen from inside the game, exactly once, so a launch and load need no key press from outside the game.
priority_reason: The one key press failed in Borg 4's unattended trial (a desktop toast took the foreground) and the maintainer had to press through; unattended runs need the bridge's own continue route, which Borg 4 moved up.

demand.note: Unattended launches: today the external key is the only route (Borg 1 to 4).

known_issues.summary: No active GSM owner/phase acceptance reader, validated Start/UI_Skip event ABI, execution-thread lifetime or one-shot compare-and-act adapter: game.continue stays refused (no_safe_route).

unknowns.question: What are the original consumers' ABI and lifetimes for an exact-once invocation in the foreground and background?
unknowns.settle_by: LC8151 to LC8156, then a separately reviewed invocation with stale, consumed, replaced and gameplay counterexamples (RB-234).

title: Launching the game through MO2
summary: The batch runner's host adapter starts the game through MO2's command line in the test profile with -skipStartScreen, waits for the bridge, and restarts it when a row needs other config.ini keys.

rows.note: Run by hand with the same command line.

quirks: The bridge is attach-only: agents launch only under the session rules, and only the test profile.
Launching MO2 minimised left a stale caption stub after it exited (Borg 2); launch it normally.

unknowns.question: Does the host adapter's launch and restart work end to end?
unknowns.settle_by: The first batch session (the ST styling batch).

notes: Borg 1 to 4 launched by hand with the MO2 command line; the adapter is offline only.

title: Quitting the game
summary: A bridge command that leaves the game through its own exit, after the save flush, so a session can end without desktop input.

demand.note: Borg 1's rule: use the game's own quit route, or a bridge quit command; CloseMainWindow acts like Alt+F4 and is the fallback.

unknowns.question: What is the shutdown and save-flush ordering, and does ExitGame exit cleanly from gameplay without a prompt?
unknowns.settle_by: Research brief (RB-234 keeps game.quit out of the current candidate)

notes: Meanwhile the batch runner's host adapter closes the game with CloseMainWindow, which Borg 4 found clean (about 25 s).

title: Graphics settings record
summary: game.options.read records the graphics and display settings (upscaler, frame generation, ray and path tracing, HDR and more) and, through the CET layer, the engine's character render options.
notes: knowledge/runtime-access.md lists it as built, not yet confirmed in game.
